To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of perlite and especially vermiculite to EPM composites improves the mechanical properties of the compounds.
the incorporation of perlite and/or vermiculite into ethylene–propylene rubber (EPR) composites significantly reduced the air and water permeability of the studied composites.
the incorporation of ionic liquid (BMIMTTF) in EPM composites containing perlite or vermiculite fillers reduces flammability, improves mechanical properties, and increases thermal conductivity.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the EPM composites containing perlite and vermiulite minerals, as well as ionic liquids, can be used as a promising material with good mechanical properties, low flammability and high thermal stability, and can be considered for applications in which the fire safety of the materials is of paramount importance.

the incorporation of perlite and/or vermiculite, with the addition of ILs, is a promising approach for the preparation of EPM composites with improved mechanical and barrier properties, and reduced flammability.

the addition of vermiculites to EPM composites is an effective way to improve the mechanical and barrier properties of EPM composites, while the incorporation of ionic liquid into EPM composites filled with perlites and vermiculites is an effective way of reducing the flammability and improving the mechanical properties of EPM composite materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perlite and vermi-culite minerals are attractive fillers for EPM composites, which can be further improved by the addition of ionic liquids.
the EPM composites with the addition of 10 phr perlite and 10 phr vermiculite, and 2.5 phr BMIMTFSIl showed a better mechanical, barrier and flammability performance than the neat EPM compound.
EPM composites filled with vermiculite and perlite are promising materials with good mechanical properties and low air permeability, which can be further enhanced by the addition of ionic liquids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of perlite and/or vermiculite fillers, in conjunction with ILs, can be an effective approach to improve the properties of elastomeric materials, such as EPM.
the use of perlite and/or vermiculite as fillers in EPM composites is an interesting and promising approach for the preparation of non-flammable and thermally insulating materials.
the EPM composite filled with perlite mineral and BMIMTFSi ionic liquid can be a good material to replace the commonly used halogenated flame retardants.
